title: "Full-Stack Audit: LLaMA-70B Training"
subtitle: "One model, six domains, twelve walls: a complete systems analysis in 60 seconds."
description: "Compose 6+ solvers across all six taxonomy domains to produce a holistic training analysis across memory capacity, compute, communication, reliability, and sustainability walls."
categories: ["capstone", "advanced"]
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import mlsysim
from mlsysim.systems.types import Fleet, Node, NetworkFabric
from mlsysim.infrastructure.registry import Grids
from mlsysim.solvers import SustainabilityModel

_model = mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B
_h100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H100
_ib_ndr = mlsysim.Systems.Fabrics.InfiniBand_NDR

_params_b = _model.parameters.to("Bparam").magnitude
_h100_cap_gb = _h100.memory.capacity.to("GB").magnitude
_h100_cap_gib = _h100.memory.capacity.to("GiB").magnitude
_h100_peak_tflops = _h100.compute.peak_flops.to("TFLOPs/s").magnitude
_nvlink_gbs = _h100.nvlink.bandwidth.to("GB/s").magnitude
_ib_gbps = _ib_ndr.bandwidth.to("Gbps").magnitude

_node = Node(
    name="DGX H100",
    accelerator=_h100,
    accelerators_per_node=8,
    intra_node_bw=_h100.nvlink.bandwidth,
)
_fabric = NetworkFabric(
    name="InfiniBand NDR",
    topology="fat-tree",
    bandwidth=_ib_ndr.bandwidth,
)
_fleet = Fleet(
    name="Training Cluster",
    node=_node,
    count=64,
    fabric=_fabric,
    region=Grids.Quebec,
)

_sust_quebec = SustainabilityModel().solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=30, datacenter=Grids.Quebec, mfu=0.4)
_sust_poland = SustainabilityModel().solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=30, datacenter=Grids.Poland, mfu=0.4)
_ci_ratio = Grids.Poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh / Grids.Quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_carbon_ratio = _sust_poland.carbon_footprint_kg / _sust_quebec.carbon_footprint_kg
```

## The Question

What does a **complete** systems analysis look like? No single solver captures the full
picture. Training a `{python} f"{_params_b:.0f}B"`-parameter model (`{python} _model.name`) on `{python} f"{_fleet.total_accelerators}"` `{python} _h100.name` GPUs involves compute walls, memory
walls, communication overhead, checkpoint I/O, energy costs, and carbon emissions,
all simultaneously. This tutorial traces all six taxonomy domains and exercises 12 of the 22
systems walls through a single workload.

::: {.callout-note}
## Prerequisites
Complete [Tutorial 0: Hello, Roofline](00_hello_roofline.qmd),
[Tutorial 1: The Memory Wall](01_memory_wall.qmd),
[Tutorial 6: Scaling to 1000 GPUs](06_scaling_1000_gpus.qmd), and
[Tutorial 9: Sensitivity Analysis](09_sensitivity.qmd). This tutorial assumes familiarity
with roofline analysis, distributed training, and binding constraint identification.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning Objectives

- **Compose** six solver families across all taxonomy domains into a holistic analysis
- **Identify** which of the 22 systems walls bind for a real training workload
- **Quantify** the hidden costs: checkpoint overhead, carbon, water, and TCO
- **Produce** a summary table mapping domain -> solver -> binding wall
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Solver Quick Reference

This capstone uses solvers from all six domains. For readers who arrived via an
accelerated learning path, the table below summarizes what each solver does:

| Solver | Domain | What It Computes |
|:-------|:-------|:-----------------|
| `SingleNodeModel` | Node | Roofline bottleneck, latency, throughput |
| `DataModel` | Data | Whether the data pipeline can sustain GPU demand |
| `ScalingModel` | Algorithm | Compute-optimal training budget (Chinchilla) |
| `DistributedModel` | Fleet | Communication overhead and scaling efficiency |
| `ReliabilityModel` | Fleet | Cluster MTBF and optimal checkpoint intervals |
| `EconomicsModel` | Ops | CapEx, OpEx, and total cost of ownership (TCO) |
| `SustainabilityModel` | Ops | Energy, carbon footprint, and water usage |
| `SensitivitySolver` | Analysis | Partial derivatives identifying the binding constraint |
| `SynthesisSolver` | Analysis | Minimum hardware specs from a latency target |
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Background: The Six Taxonomy Domains

The MLSys wall taxonomy organizes 22 systems walls into six domains:

| Domain | Walls | What It Covers |
|:-------|:------|:---------------|
| Node | 1--3 | Compute, memory capacity, memory bandwidth |
| Data | 8--10 | Storage throughput, data pipeline stalls |
| Algorithm | 11--13 | Scaling laws, compute-optimal training |
| Fleet | 14--16 | Communication, synchronization, reliability |
| Ops | 17--20 | TCO, energy, carbon, water, safety |
| Analysis | 21--22 | Sensitivity, inverse synthesis |

No single solver spans all six. The insight emerges from **composition**.
:::

---

## 1. Setup: Build the Fleet

We construct a `{python} f"{_fleet.total_accelerators}"`-GPU training cluster: `{python} f"{_fleet.count}"` `{python} _node.name` nodes, `{python} f"{_node.accelerators_per_node}"` GPUs per node,
NVLink intra-node (`{python} f"{_nvlink_gbs:.0f} GB/s"`), InfiniBand NDR inter-node (`{python} f"{_ib_gbps:.0f} Gbps"`), powered by `{python} Grids.Quebec.name`'s hydroelectric grid (`{python} f"{Grids.Quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} g CO2/kWh"`).

```python
import mlsysim
from mlsysim.systems.types import Fleet, Node, NetworkFabric
from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
```

```{python}
from mlsysim.systems.types import Fleet, Node, NetworkFabric
from mlsysim.infrastructure.registry import Grids
from mlsysim.core.units import Q_

model = mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B
h100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H100
ib_ndr = mlsysim.Systems.Fabrics.InfiniBand_NDR

# Build the DGX H100 node: 8 GPUs connected by NVLink 4.0
node = Node(
    name="DGX H100",
    accelerator=h100,
    accelerators_per_node=8,
    intra_node_bw=h100.nvlink.bandwidth
)

# Build the cluster fabric: InfiniBand NDR
fabric = NetworkFabric(
    name="InfiniBand NDR",
    topology="fat-tree",
    bandwidth=ib_ndr.bandwidth
)

# Build the fleet: 64 nodes = 512 GPUs, Quebec grid
fleet = Fleet(
    name="Training Cluster",
    node=node,
    count=64,
    fabric=fabric,
    region=Grids.Quebec
)

from mlsysim.show import table, info, banner

info("Fleet Configuration",
     Model=f"{model.name} ({model.parameters.to('Bparam'):.1f~})",
     Fleet=f"{fleet.count} nodes x {node.accelerators_per_node} GPUs = {fleet.total_accelerators} GPUs",
     Intra_node=f"NVLink 4.0 ({h100.nvlink.bandwidth.to('GB/s'):.0f~})",
     Inter_node=f"IB NDR ({ib_ndr.bandwidth.to('Gbps'):.0f~})",
     Region=Grids.Quebec.name)
```

---

## 2. Node (Walls 1--3): Single-GPU Roofline

The first step evaluates an unsharded `{python} model.name` forward pass on a single `{python} h100.name` GPU.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import SingleNodeModel

node_solver = SingleNodeModel()
node_result = node_solver.solve(
    model=model, hardware=h100,
    batch_size=4, precision="fp16"
)

banner("Domain: Node (Walls 1-3)")
info(Feasible=node_result.feasible,
     Required_memory=node_result.memory_footprint.to('GB'),
     Available_memory=h100.memory.capacity.to('GB'),
     Bottleneck=node_result.bottleneck,
     Per_GPU_latency=node_result.latency.to('ms'),
     Throughput=f"{node_result.throughput.to('1/s').magnitude:.1f} samples/s")
```

At `{python} f"{model.parameters.to('Bparam').magnitude:.1f}B"` parameters, `{python} model.name` weights alone require `{python} f"{node_result.memory_footprint.to('GB'):~.1f}"` in FP16, exceeding a single `{python} h100.name`'s `{python} f"{_h100_cap_gib:.0f} GiB"` (`{python} f"{_h100_cap_gb:.1f} GB"`) HBM capacity (`feasible = `{python} f"{node_result.feasible}"``). Because the unsharded model spills across PCIe (`{python} f"{node_result.offload_effective_bw.to('GB/s'):~.0f}"`), `SingleNodeModel` reports **`{python} node_result.bottleneck`**-bound at `{python} f"{node_result.latency.to('ms'):~.1f}"` per step (`{python} f"{node_result.throughput.to('1/s').magnitude:.1f}"` samples/s).

Wall 2 (Memory Capacity) and Wall 3 (Memory Bandwidth) immediately rule out unsharded single-GPU execution and force intra-node tensor parallelism (`TP=8` in Section 5). The next question is whether the storage and preprocessing pipeline can keep up with `{python} f"{fleet.total_accelerators}"` GPUs demanding training tokens.

---

## 3. Data (Walls 8--10): Whether the Pipeline Can Keep Up

The storage and preprocessing pipeline must deliver tokenized batches at least as fast as the cluster consumes them. If it cannot, the GPUs stall.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import DataModel

# Estimate data demand per step: 4 samples/GPU * 512 GPUs * 2048 tokens * 2 bytes ≈ 8 MB/step
data_demand = Q_("8 MB/s")

data_solver = DataModel()
data_result = data_solver.solve(
    workload_data_rate=data_demand,
    hardware=h100
)

banner("Domain: Data (Walls 8-10)")
info(Data_demand=data_result.demand_bw,
     Data_supply=data_result.supply_bw,
     Utilization=f"{data_result.utilization:.2%}",
     Stalled=data_result.is_stalled,
     Bottleneck=data_result.bottleneck)
```

At `{python} f"{data_result.demand_bw.to('MB/s'):~.0f}"` demand against `{python} f"{data_result.supply_bw.to('GB/s'):~.1f}"` storage bandwidth, storage utilization is only `{python} f"{data_result.utilization:.2%}"` (`is_stalled = `{python} f"{data_result.is_stalled}"``). For text-based training, the data pipeline is rarely the bottleneck because tokenized text is compact; for image or video training, this wall can dominate.

The remaining question is whether the 30-day compute budget on `{python} f"{fleet.total_accelerators}"` GPUs is allocated optimally according to scaling laws.

---

## 4. Algorithm (Walls 11--13): Compute-Optimal Budget

The test of whether this training budget is compute-optimal is the Chinchilla scaling
law, which prescribes $D = 20P$ (tokens = $20\times$ parameters) for optimal allocation.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import ScalingModel

# MFU (Model FLOP Utilization): the fraction of peak hardware FLOP/s that goes
# to useful model computation (excluding communication, idle time, overhead).
# MFU = 0.4 means 40% of theoretical peak.
gpu_flops = h100.compute.peak_flops.to("flop/s").magnitude
total_flops = fleet.total_accelerators * gpu_flops * 30 * 86400 * 0.4
compute_budget = Q_(total_flops, "flop")

scaling_solver = ScalingModel()
scaling_result = scaling_solver.solve(
    compute_budget=compute_budget,
    target_model_size=model.parameters
)

banner("Domain: Algorithm (Walls 11-13)")
info(Compute_budget=compute_budget.to('EFLOP'),
     Optimal_tokens=f"{scaling_result.optimal_tokens.magnitude:.2e}",
     Tokens_per_parameter=f"{scaling_result.tokens_per_parameter:.1f}",
     Chinchilla_ratio=f"{'OVER' if scaling_result.tokens_per_parameter > 20 else 'UNDER'}-trained")
```

With `{python} f"{fleet.total_accelerators}"` GPUs at `{python} f"{_h100_peak_tflops:.0f} TFLOP/s"` peak FP16 and 40% MFU over 30 days, the compute budget reaches `{python} f"{compute_budget.to('EFLOP'):~.0f}"`, funding `{python} f"{scaling_result.optimal_tokens.magnitude / 1e12:.2f}T"` tokens (`{python} f"{scaling_result.tokens_per_parameter:.1f}"` tokens per parameter, slightly below the Chinchilla 20 tokens/parameter ratio). If the tokens-per-parameter ratio is significantly above or below 20, the training budget is not optimally allocated: over-training wastes compute, while under-training wastes model capacity.

---

## 5. Fleet (Walls 14--16): Communication and Reliability

Sharding `{python} model.name` with `TP=8` within each `{python} node.name` node (`PP=1`, `DP=64` across the `{python} f"{fleet.count}"` nodes) divides the weights across 8 GPUs per replica. The distributed solver models both the replica's 2,048-token forward-backward pass and the AllReduce communication overhead, while the reliability solver computes cluster MTBF and optimal checkpoint intervals.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import DistributedModel, ReliabilityModel

# 3D parallelism: TP=8 (within node), PP=1, DP=64
dist_solver = DistributedModel()
dist_result = dist_solver.solve(
    model=model, fleet=fleet,
    batch_size=2048, precision="fp16",
    tp_size=8, pp_size=1,
    overlap_comm=True, seq_len=2048
)

banner("Domain: Fleet (Walls 14-16)")
info(Replica_bottleneck=dist_result.node_profile.bottleneck,
     Replica_compute_latency=dist_result.node_profile.latency.to('ms'),
     Scaling_efficiency=f"{dist_result.scaling_efficiency:.2%}",
     Step_latency=dist_result.step_latency_total.to('ms'),
     DP_comm_latency=dist_result.dp_communication_latency.to('ms'),
     TP_comm_latency=dist_result.tp_communication_latency.to('ms'),
     Bubble_fraction=f"{dist_result.bubble_fraction:.2%}")
```

```{python}
# Reliability: 30-day training job
rel_solver = ReliabilityModel()
rel_result = rel_solver.solve(
    fleet=fleet,
    job_duration_hours=30*24,
    checkpoint_time_s=120
)

info(Fleet_MTBF=rel_result.fleet_mtbf.to('hour'),
     Failure_probability=f"{rel_result.failure_probability:.2%}",
     Expected_failures=f"{rel_result.expected_failures:.1f}",
     Optimal_ckpt_interval=rel_result.optimal_checkpoint_interval.to('minute'))
```

With `TP=8` across each node, the 2,048-token forward-backward pass is **`{python} dist_result.node_profile.bottleneck`**-bound (`{python} f"{dist_result.node_profile.latency.to('ms'):~.1f}"` replica compute latency), and overlapping DP AllReduce (`{python} f"{dist_result.dp_communication_latency.to('ms'):~.1f}"` unoverlapped) with backward compute plus intra-node TP AllReduce (`{python} f"{dist_result.tp_communication_latency.to('ms'):~.1f}"`) yields a `{python} f"{dist_result.step_latency_total.to('ms'):~.1f}"` step time and **`{python} f"{dist_result.scaling_efficiency:.2%}"`** scaling efficiency.

At `{python} f"{fleet.total_accelerators}"` GPUs, however, the cluster MTBF shrinks to **`{python} f"{rel_result.fleet_mtbf.to('hour'):~.1f}"`**, with **`{python} f"{rel_result.expected_failures:.1f}"`** expected failures over the 30-day run (`{python} f"{rel_result.failure_probability:.2%}"` failure probability) and an optimal Young-Daly checkpoint interval of **`{python} f"{rel_result.optimal_checkpoint_interval.to('minute'):~.1f}"`**. Checkpoint overhead and rollback recovery become a non-trivial fraction of wall-clock time---the hidden cost that single-node analysis misses entirely.

---

## 6. Ops (Walls 17--20): TCO, Energy, Carbon, Water

The economics solver combines CapEx, OpEx, and sustainability into a single financial model.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import EconomicsModel, SustainabilityModel

# 30-day training run
econ_solver = EconomicsModel()
econ_result = econ_solver.solve(
    fleet=fleet,
    duration_days=30,
    grid=Grids.Quebec,
    mfu=0.4
)

banner("Domain: Ops (Walls 17-20)")
info(CapEx=f"${econ_result.capex_usd:,.0f}",
     OpEx_energy=f"${econ_result.opex_energy_usd:,.0f}",
     OpEx_maintenance=f"${econ_result.opex_maintenance_usd:,.0f}",
     Total_TCO=f"${econ_result.tco_usd:,.0f}")
```

```{python}
sust_solver = SustainabilityModel()
sust_result = sust_solver.solve(
    fleet=fleet,
    duration_days=30,
    datacenter=Grids.Quebec,
    mfu=0.4
)

info(IT_Energy=sust_result.it_energy_kwh.to('MWh'),
     Total_Energy_PUE=sust_result.total_energy_kwh.to('MWh'),
     Carbon_footprint=f"{sust_result.carbon_footprint_kg:.0f} kg CO2",
     Water_usage=f"{sust_result.water_usage_liters:.0f} liters",
     PUE=sust_result.pue,
     Region=sust_result.region_name)
```

For the 30-day run, `EconomicsModel` reports **`{python} f"${econ_result.tco_usd:,.0f}"`** in total TCO (`{python} f"${econ_result.capex_usd:,.0f}"` amortized CapEx, `{python} f"${econ_result.opex_energy_usd:,.0f}"` energy OpEx, and `{python} f"${econ_result.opex_maintenance_usd:,.0f}"` maintenance OpEx). `{python} Grids.Quebec.name`'s hydroelectric grid (`{python} f"{Grids.Quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} g CO2/kWh"`, PUE `{python} f"{sust_result.pue:.2f}"`) keeps total emissions to **`{python} f"{sust_result.carbon_footprint_kg:,.0f} kg CO2"`** (`{python} f"{sust_result.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000:.1f} tonnes"` across `{python} f"{sust_result.total_energy_kwh.to('MWh'):~.1f}"` of facility energy). The same run in Poland (`{python} f"{Grids.Poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} g CO2/kWh"`, PUE `{python} f"{Grids.Poland.pue:.2f}"`) produces **`{python} f"{_sust_poland.carbon_footprint_kg:,.0f} kg CO2"`** (`{python} f"{_sust_poland.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000:.1f} tonnes"`, `{python} f"{_carbon_ratio:.0f}×"` higher), making infrastructure geography a first-class engineering variable.

---

## 7. Analysis (Walls 21--22): Sensitivity and Synthesis

Finally, run `SensitivitySolver` on a single `{python} h100.name` and `SynthesisSolver` for a 200 ms step latency target.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import SensitivitySolver, SynthesisSolver

# Sensitivity: check the single-GPU binding constraint for unsharded Llama-3.1-70B
sens_solver = SensitivitySolver()
sens_result = sens_solver.solve(
    model=model, hardware=h100, precision="fp16"
)

banner("Domain: Analysis (Walls 21-22)")
info(Binding_constraint=sens_result.binding_constraint)

sens_rows = [[param, f"{val:+.4f}"] for param, val in sens_result.sensitivities.items()]
table(["Parameter", "Sensitivity"], sens_rows)
```

```{python}
# Synthesis: minimum hardware specs for a 200 ms single-step target
synth_solver = SynthesisSolver()
synth_result = synth_solver.solve(
    model=model,
    target_latency=Q_("200 ms"),   # per-GPU step target
    precision="fp16"
)

info("Synthesis (200ms step target)",
     Required_BW=synth_result.required_bw.to('TB/s'),
     Required_FLOPS=synth_result.required_flops.to('TFLOPs/s'),
     Required_memory=synth_result.required_memory.to('GB'))
```

On an unsharded single `{python} h100.name`, `SensitivitySolver` identifies **`{python} sens_result.binding_constraint`** as the binding constraint because the `{python} f"{synth_result.required_memory.to('GB'):~.1f}"` FP16 weight footprint exceeds `{python} f"{_h100_cap_gib:.0f} GiB"` (`{python} f"{_h100_cap_gb:.1f} GB"`), pinning all small local perturbations at PCIe offload bandwidth until model parallelism (`TP=8`) brings the per-GPU footprint inside HBM.

---

## 8. Summary Table: The Complete Picture

We have now traced a single workload through all six domains. Each solver answered one
question in isolation. The systems engineer's job, however, is synthesis: seeing the complete
picture at once. The table below is that picture, and its most important property is
that no single row captures the full story.

```{python}
mtbf_hours = rel_result.fleet_mtbf.to('hour').magnitude
summary_rows = [
    ["Node",      "SingleNodeModel",      f"Bottleneck: {node_result.bottleneck}",              "Wall 2/3: Memory"],
    ["Data",      "DataModel",            f"Util: {data_result.utilization:.2%}",               "Not binding"],
    ["Algorithm", "ScalingModel",         f"Tok/param: {scaling_result.tokens_per_parameter:.1f}","Wall 11"],
    ["Fleet",     "DistributedModel",     f"Efficiency: {dist_result.scaling_efficiency:.0%}",   "Wall 14: Comm"],
    ["Fleet",     "ReliabilityModel",     f"MTBF: {mtbf_hours:.0f}h",                           "Wall 16: Ckpt"],
    ["Ops",       "EconomicsModel",       f"TCO: ${econ_result.tco_usd:,.0f}",                  "Wall 19: Cost"],
    ["Ops",       "SustainabilityModel",  f"CO2: {sust_result.carbon_footprint_kg:.0f} kg",     "Wall 18: Carbon"],
    ["Analysis",  "SensitivitySolver",    f"Binding: {sens_result.binding_constraint}",         "Wall 21"],
]

table(["Domain", "Solver", "Key Metric", "Binding Wall"], summary_rows, "<<>>")
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Key Insight

**No single solver captures the full picture; the systems view emerges from composition.**
This end-to-end trace exercises 12 of 22 walls through a single model. At the single-GPU level,
memory capacity (`{python} f"{synth_result.required_memory.to('GB'):~.1f}"` vs. `{python} f"{_h100_cap_gib:.0f} GiB"`) forces tensor parallelism (`TP=8`), where each 8-GPU replica is compute-bound (`{python} f"{dist_result.node_profile.latency.to('ms'):~.0f}"` per step at `{python} f"{dist_result.scaling_efficiency:.0%}"` scaling efficiency). The **hidden costs** only appear at fleet scale:
a `{python} f"{rel_result.fleet_mtbf.to('hour'):~.1f}"` cluster MTBF forces checkpoints every `{python} f"{rel_result.optimal_checkpoint_interval.to('minute'):~.0f}"`, and infrastructure geography (`{python} Grids.Quebec.name` vs. `{python} Grids.Poland.name`) changes grid carbon intensity by `{python} f"{_ci_ratio:.0f}×"` and PUE-adjusted carbon emissions by `{python} f"{_carbon_ratio:.0f}×"` (as [Tutorial 7](07_geography.qmd) demonstrated). A complete
systems analysis is not one solver run but the composition of all six domains.
:::
